title: Suspension in the module projective model is the cochain shift
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring, and equip all unbounded $R$-module cochain complexes with the projective model structure of [lem-coef-projective-cochain-monoidal-model], using [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] for cochains, quasi-isomorphisms and shifts. Thus $Q[1]^n=Q^{n+1}$ with differential $-d_Q$. For every cofibrant complex $Q$, form $C(Q)^n=Q^n\oplus Q^{n+1}$ with differential $(b,a)\mapsto(d_Qb+a,-d_Qa)$ and inclusion $Q\to C(Q)$ given by $b\mapsto(b,0)$. This inclusion is a cofibration and $C(Q)$ is cofibrant and contractible. The span $C(Q)\leftarrow Q\to C(Q)$ represents the span $0\leftarrow Q\to0$ in the homotopy coherent localization. Its ordinary pushout has terms $Q^n\oplus Q^{n+1}\oplus Q^{n+1}$ and differential $(b,a_1,a_2)\mapsto(d_Qb+a_1+a_2,-d_Qa_1,-d_Qa_2)$. Projection $(b,a_1,a_2)\mapsto a_2$ is a quasi-isomorphism from this pushout to $Q[1]$, natural in maps of cofibrant complexes. Consequently the suspension induced on the ordinary homotopy category is naturally isomorphic to $[1]$. The homotopy coherent localization is stable in the sense of [lem-coef-pointed-model-stability]: it has a zero object and finite homotopy limits and colimits, and a square is a homotopy pushout if and only if it is a homotopy pullback.

proof.text: The cofibration characterization of [lem-coef-projective-cochain-monoidal-model] applied to $0\to Q$ says that $Q$ has projective terms and $\underline{\mathrm{Hom}}(Q,N)$ is acyclic for every acyclic $N$. The same holds for $Q[1]$. Its terms are reindexed projectives. A degree-$r$ Hom cochain $u:Q[1]\to N$ reindexes as $v^j=u^{j-1}$ of degree $r-1$ from $Q$ to $N$. Both Hom differentials then have formula $d_Nv+(-1)^rvd_Q$. Thus a cycle corresponds to a cycle, and a primitive in degree $r-2$ reindexes to a primitive in degree $r-1$. This proves acyclicity without a boundedness assumption. Hence $Q[1]$ is dg-projective and cofibrant.

proof.text: Use the cone and shift conventions of [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. The displayed $C(Q)$ is the cone of $1_Q$; squaring its differential gives $(d_Q^2b+d_Qa-d_Qa,d_Q^2a)=0$. Its degree-minus-one map $h(b,a)=(0,b)$ satisfies $dh+hd=1$. In particular every cycle $z$ is the boundary $d(hz)$, so $C(Q)\to0$ is a quasi-isomorphism. Its terms are projective: maps from $Q^n\oplus Q^{n+1}$ lift across a module surjection by lifting each summand. Moreover for a degree-$r$ cochain $u:C(Q)\to N$, the operator $H(u)=(-1)^ruh$ satisfies $\delta H+H\delta=1$ on its Hom complex. Thus that Hom complex is acyclic for every $N$, and $C(Q)$ is dg-projective. By [lem-coef-projective-cochain-monoidal-model], $C(Q)$ is cofibrant. The inclusion $i(b)=(b,0)$ is a chain map, split in each degree, with cokernel exactly $Q[1]$; Step 1 and the same cofibration characterization make $i$ a cofibration.

proof.text: The category of complexes has a zero complex, simultaneously initial and terminal, by the unique degreewise zero maps. The model from [lem-coef-projective-cochain-monoidal-model] is combinatorial, so in particular complete and cocomplete with functorial model factorizations. Therefore [lem-coef-pointed-model-stability] applies. The maps $C(Q)\to0$, with identity at the central vertex $Q$, give an objectwise weak equivalence from $C(Q)\leftarrow Q\to C(Q)$ to $0\leftarrow Q\to0$. They become equivalences in the coherent localization. All three objects in the first span are cofibrant and both outgoing maps are cofibrations by Steps 1--2. The cited pointed-model theorem consequently identifies its ordinary pushout with the homotopy pushout, hence with $\Sigma Q$.

proof.text: Compute the ordinary pushout as $(C(Q)\oplus C(Q))/\{((q,0),(-q,0)):q\in Q\}$ degreewise. The map $((b_1,a_1),(b_2,a_2))\mapsto(b_1+b_2,a_1,a_2)$ identifies this quotient with $P(Q)^n=Q^n\oplus Q^{n+1}\oplus Q^{n+1}$; its inverse sends $(b,a_1,a_2)$ to the class of $((b,a_1),(0,a_2))$. Each pair of chain maps from $C(Q)$ agreeing on $Q$ factors uniquely through this quotient, so it is the pushout as complexes, not just as graded modules. Applying the two cone differentials and adding their first coordinates gives precisely $d_P(b,a_1,a_2)=(d_Qb+a_1+a_2,-d_Qa_1,-d_Qa_2)$.

proof.text: The projection $p:P(Q)\to Q[1]$, $p(b,a_1,a_2)=a_2$, is a chain map. It has the chain-map section $s(a)=(0,-a,a)$: $d_Ps(a)=(0,d_Qa,-d_Qa)=s(-d_Qa)$. Its kernel consists of $(b,a_1,0)$ with the cone differential, so is exactly $C(Q)$. More explicitly $P(Q)\cong C(Q)\oplus Q[1]$ by $(b,a_1,a_2)\mapsto((b,a_1+a_2),a_2)$, with inverse $((b,t),a)\mapsto(b,t-a,a)$. Step 2 contracts the first summand. Thus $ps=1$ and $1-sp=d_PH+Hd_P$, where $H(b,a_1,a_2)=(0,b,0)$. On cohomology these identities make $H^r(p)$ and $H^r(s)$ inverse: a homotopy term on a cycle is a boundary. Hence $p$ is a quasi-isomorphism in every degree.

proof.text: For a chain map $f:Q\to Q'$ between cofibrant complexes, the cone map is $(b,a)\mapsto(fb,fa)$ and the pushout map is $(b,a_1,a_2)\mapsto(fb,fa_1,fa_2)$. These commute with both inclusions and with $p,s,H$ by coordinatewise substitution. Thus Steps 3--5 identify suspension naturally with $[1]$ on localized cofibrant complexes. To see this covers the ordinary homotopy category on all complexes, take a functorial cofibrant replacement $q_X:FX\to X$ using the model factorizations of [lem-coef-projective-cochain-monoidal-model]. Naturality and two-out-of-three imply that $F$ preserves weak equivalences. On localizations, $q$ identifies the composite inclusion followed by replacement with the identity, and its restriction to cofibrants identifies the other composite with the identity. These localized categories are therefore equivalent. The pointed-model theorem [lem-coef-pointed-model-stability] identifies the homotopy category with ordinary localization, so the same natural comparison is $\Sigma\cong[1]$ there.

proof.text: The cochain shift has inverse $[-1]$, where $(X[-1])^n=X^{n-1}$ with differential $-d_X$. Both composites cancel the two negative signs and reindex back to $X$. Shifts preserve quasi-isomorphisms, since their cycles and boundaries are exactly the reindexed cycles and boundaries, so these mutually inverse functors descend to the ordinary localization. Step 6 makes suspension an equivalence on that localization. The criterion of [lem-coef-pointed-model-stability] now implies stability of the homotopy coherent localization. The same theorem supplies its zero object and finite homotopy limits and colimits, and says exactly that homotopy pushout squares and homotopy pullback squares coincide.
